contexts.text: To take of the tree of lives, and eat () = to know, even to acknowledgement, whatever is of love and faith.
He was no more, for God took him () = that that doctrine was preserved for the use of posterity.
Take thou unto thee of all food that is eaten () = goods and delights. AC 678.
That he took nothing of the truth of good. Signified. To eat = to appropriate, thus to take; for that which is appropriated from another is taken from him.
He took her, and lay with her () = ... to be conjoined...
What man can acquire such (revelations) from himself?
Therefore both taken together are called love...
For that which has been taken from something else, retains from what is proper to it that which it makes its own.
A man can receive nothing unless it be given him from Heaven (). Explained.
